NOTE: pointer numbering does not match the arXiv source: Table 1 here is 'Mass Estimates ... based on 1D fit' (no positions); the mass-peak positions are in §4.1 ('Two-dimensional Mass Reconstruction') and §4.2 ('Significance and Locations of the Weak-Lensing Mass Peaks'); Fig. 5 = mass map, Fig. 7 = centroid comparison overlay, Fig. 8 = bootstrap centroid distribution (figure numbers counted from the LaTeX order).

z_cl.quote: We present a {\it Hubble Space Telescope} weak-lensing study of the merging galaxy cluster ``El Gordo'' (\elgordo)~at $z=0.87$

I.location: §4.1 'Two-dimensional Mass Reconstruction', paragraph after Fig. 8; same position (more digits) in Fig. 8 caption (bootstrap centroid figure)
I.quote: The shear peaks are located at R.A.=01:02:50.60, Decl.=$-$49:15:04.5 for the NW component and R.A.=01:02:56.31, Delc.=$-$49:16:23.2 for the SE one.  ; Fig. 8 caption: "The (0,0) positions correspond to positions of R.A.=01:02:50.601, Decl.=$-$49:15:04.48 for the NW component and R.A.=01:02:56.312, Delc.=$-$49:16:23.15 for the SE one."

uncertainty.quote: The centroids of both components are tightly constrained ($\mytilde4\arcsec$) and close to the optical luminosity centers.

alternatives.qualifier: <~ (upper bound), MCMC 2-NFW-halo centroid, not the kappa-map peak
alternatives.quote: In Figure~\ref{fig_centroid}, we display the centroid distributions of the two halos, which illustrate that the mass centroid is well-constrained ($\lesssim3\arcsec$).

uncertainty.caveat: Paper does not say whether ~4" is a 1D sigma, a radius, or per-axis; bootstrap 1/2-sigma contours are only shown graphically (Fig. 8; SE distribution 'elongated east-west').

G.type: X-ray peak (single Chandra X-ray peak, located close to the SE mass peak)
G.location: §4.2 'Significance and Locations of the Weak-Lensing Mass Peaks'; also Abstract
G.quote: The X-ray emission is strongest near this SE mass peak. The distance between the X-ray and SE mass peaks is $\mytilde8\arcsec$.  Based on the above bootstrapping analysis, the significance of the offset is at the $\mytilde2\sigma$ level.  ; Abstract: "The X-ray and mass peaks are spatially offset by $\mytilde8\arcsec$ ($\mytilde100\hubblem$ kpc), which is significant at the $\mytilde2\sigma$ confidence level."
G.uncertainty_context: Only the offset significance (~2 sigma, from bootstrapping the lensing centroid) is given; no X-ray centroiding error is stated. NOTE: offset is from I (the protocol schema lists 'G'|'S' as reference; here the reference is I).

notes: I: absolute position given. G: only a stated I-G separation of ~8" (~100 h^-1 kpc), ~2 sigma significance. S: no luminosity-weighted centroid tabulated and no BCG position given anywhere; only 'luminosity peak' (qualitatively 'close to' the SE mass peak, used as halo centre in 1D fits and in Fig. 7 'Various measures of the cluster centroids are shown as illustrated') - positions only in figures, not reportable. I uncertainty: abstract '~4"' (type unspecified) and MCMC '<~3"'; no G or S uncertainty. Pointer section/table numbers (§3.2-3.3, Table 1, Fig. 3-4) do not correspond to the arXiv source numbering; content used is §4.1-4.3, Figs 5/7/8.
